traits.carpels.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 262, 264: general formula 2 to 5, up to 10 carpels; Celastrales tend to tricarpellate gynoecia.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 262, 264: 4-5 free, large petals (general formula C (3) 4-5 (6), not fused). Free petals: rotate by PlantGen's free-petal rule; the book names no other corolla form.

traits.hypanthium.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 262: Ronse De Craene (Celastrales): a short hypanthium is occasionally present, linked with a half-inferior ovary.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 180 Celastraceae: trees, shrubs or climbers; leaves alternate or opposite, simple; stipules small and soon falling, or none (so left unstated); flowers mostly in cymes or clusters, small, regular; calyx 4- or 5-lobed, petals 5, rarely none; stamens 4 or 5, alternate with the petals, on or below a fleshy disc; ovary superior; fruit of many kinds (capsules in Euonymus and Celastrus, drupes, berries, samaras), so left unstated. APG's family also takes in the herb Parnassia, hence herbaceous as rare.
